title: 1 John Chapter 3 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 John chapter 3 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 John Chapter 3 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 John Chapter 3.

questions.question: In 1 John 3, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us
And ye know that he was manifested to take away our sins
Whosoever abideth in him sinneth not
Little children, let no man deceive you
questions.correctAnswer: Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us
questions.explanation: This phrase is the very first statement in 1 John 3:1.

questions.question: What are we called according to 1 John 3:1?
questions.explanation: The verse states that we should be called the sons of God (1 John 3:1).

questions.question: What does it mean that the world knoweth us not according to 1 John 3:1?
options: Because we are not from this world
Because we do not speak its language
questions.explanation: The verse states that the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not (1 John 3:1).

questions.question: What does 1 John 3:2 say about what we shall be when He appears?
questions.explanation: The verse states that when He shall appear, we shall be like Him (1 John 3:2).

questions.question: According to 1 John 3:3, what does every man that hath this hope do?
questions.explanation: The verse states that every man that hath this hope in him purifieth himself (1 John 3:3).

questions.question: What is sin according to 1 John 3:4?
questions.explanation: The verse defines sin as the transgression of the law (1 John 3:4).

questions.question: What do we know about Him according to 1 John 3:5?
options: He was manifested to take away our sins
questions.correctAnswer: He was manifested to take away our sins
questions.explanation: The verse states that He was manifested to take away our sins (1 John 3:5).

questions.question: What is stated about whosoever abideth in Him in 1 John 3:6?
questions.explanation: The verse states that whosoever abideth in Him sinneth not (1 John 3:6).

questions.question: What does 1 John 3:7 advise little children about deception?
questions.explanation: The verse specifically advises little children to let no man deceive you (1 John 3:7).

questions.question: According to 1 John 3:8, who is he that committeth sin?
questions.explanation: The verse states that he that committeth sin is of the devil (1 John 3:8).

questions.question: What was the purpose of the Son of God being manifested according to 1 John 3:8?
options: To destroy the works of the devil
questions.correctAnswer: To destroy the works of the devil
questions.explanation: The verse states that the purpose was to destroy the works of the devil (1 John 3:8).

questions.question: True or False: We are called the sons of God.
questions.explanation: The verse states that we should be called the sons of God (1 John 3:1).

questions.question: True or False: In Him is no sin.
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that in Him is no sin (1 John 3:5).

questions.question: True or False: He that committeth sin is of the light.
questions.explanation: The text does not state that he that committeth sin is of the light; instead, it states he is of the devil (1 John 3:8).

questions.question: True or False: Little children are encouraged to deceive others.
questions.explanation: The text advises little children to let no man deceive you, not to deceive others (1 John 3:7).

medium.title: 1 John Chapter 3 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 John Chapter 3 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin; what is the reason given in 1 John 3:9?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is from 1 John 3:9, which states that 'for his seed remaineth in him: and he cannot sin, because he is born of God.' This indicates that being born of God gives one a new nature that prevents sinning.

questions.question: What does 1 John 3:10 promise will happen if someone does not do righteousness?
options: They are a child of the devil
questions.correctAnswer: They are a child of the devil
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:10 states that 'whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother.' This shows that failing to do righteousness aligns one with the devil.

questions.question: According to 1 John 3:11, what is the message that was heard from the beginning?
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:11 clearly states, 'For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another.' This emphasizes the importance of love among believers.

questions.question: What does 1 John 3:12 compare the behavior of believers with?
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:12 refers to Cain as 'who was of that wicked one,' contrasting Cain's evil actions with the expected behavior of believers who are called to love.

questions.question: According to 1 John 3:13, what should believers not be surprised about?
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:13 states, 'Marvel not, my brethren, if the world hate you.' This verse encourages believers to understand that hatred from the world is a common experience.

questions.question: What do we know about those who love their brothers according to 1 John 3:14?
options: They have passed from death unto life
questions.correctAnswer: They have passed from death unto life
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:14 states, 'We know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love the brethren.' This highlights love as evidence of spiritual life.

questions.question: According to 1 John 3:15, who is considered a murderer?
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:15 states, 'Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer,' emphasizing the seriousness of hatred in relation to the sanctity of life.

questions.question: What does 1 John 3:16 say we should do because of God's love for us?
options: Lay down our lives for the brethren
questions.correctAnswer: Lay down our lives for the brethren
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:16 explains that 'Hereby perceive we the love of God, because he laid down his life for us: and we ought to lay down our lives for the brethren.' This indicates a call to selfless love.

questions.question: What does 1 John 3:1 reveal about the love the Father has for us?
options: It allows us to be called sons of God
questions.correctAnswer: It allows us to be called sons of God
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:1 states, 'Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God.' This emphasizes the transformative nature of God's love.

questions.question: What does 1 John 3:4 say sin is?
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:4 defines sin as 'for sin is the transgression of the law,' indicating that sin violates God's standards.

questions.question: What does 1 John 3:7 encourage believers not to be deceived about?
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:7 warns believers, 'let no man deceive you: he that doeth righteousness is righteous, even as he is righteous.' This stresses the importance of living righteously.

questions.question: What does 1 John 3:8 indicate about the purpose of the Son of God?
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:8 states, 'For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil.' This indicates that Jesus came to address sin directly.

questions.question: Is it true that every person who commits sin is of the devil according to 1 John 3:8?
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:8 states, 'He that committeth sin is of the devil.' This describes a fundamental principle about sin and its origin.

questions.question: Is it false that the children of God are recognized by their hatred for their brothers according to 1 John 3:10?
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:10 indicates that 'whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother.' Thus, hatred is not a mark of God's children.

questions.question: Is it false that love among believers is optional according to 1 John 3:11?
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:11 emphasizes that loving one another is not optional but a command, 'For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another.'

hard.title: 1 John Chapter 3 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 John Chapter 3.

questions.question: What happens to the love of God in a person who sees his brother in need but shuts up his compassion?
options: It does not dwell in him
questions.correctAnswer: It does not dwell in him
questions.explanation: This is stated in 1 John 3:17, which questions how the love of God can dwell in someone who lacks compassion for others.

questions.question: According to 1 John 3:18, how should we love?
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:18 emphasizes that love should be expressed through actions and sincerity, not just words.

questions.question: What does 1 John 3:19 assure us of?
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:19 states that our actions help us to know we belong to the truth and can assure our hearts before God.

questions.question: What is said about God in relation to our hearts in 1 John 3:20?
options: He is greater than our hearts
He is indifferent to our hearts
questions.correctAnswer: He is greater than our hearts
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:20 affirms that God knows all things and is greater than our own self-condemnation.

questions.question: What confidence do we have towards God if our heart does not condemn us, according to 1 John 3:21?
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:21 states that if our heart does not condemn us, we have confidence in our relationship with God.

questions.question: What commandment is given in 1 John 3:23?
options: To believe on the name of Jesus and love one another
questions.correctAnswer: To believe on the name of Jesus and love one another
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:23 outlines the essential commandment to believe in Jesus and to love one another as He commanded.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'agape' in 1 John 3:18 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Agape' refers to a selfless, unconditional love that is the foundation of God's love for us, as highlighted in 1 John 3:18.

questions.question: What literary device is employed in 1 John 3:17 regarding compassion?
questions.explanation: The structure of 1 John 3:17 uses parallelism to contrast having goods with the action of showing compassion.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects with the theme of loving one's brother as stated in 1 John 3:11?
questions.explanation: John 15:12 echoes 1 John 3:11 by emphasizing the command to love one another as Jesus has loved us.

questions.question: Which passage from the Old Testament resonates with the message of compassion found in 1 John 3:17?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 19:17 highlights the act of helping the poor as lending to the Lord, aligning with the theme of compassion in 1 John 3:17.

questions.question: What precedes the statement in 1 John 3:20 regarding God's knowledge of our hearts?
options: The command to love one another
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:19, which discusses knowing we are of the truth, precedes 1 John 3:20 about God's greater knowledge of our hearts.

questions.question: Which verse describes the nature of sin and its relation to the law in 1 John 3?
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:4 defines sin as the transgression of the law, establishing a biblical foundation for understanding sin.

questions.question: The statement in 1 John 3:16 about laying down one’s life for the brethren reflects which key concept?
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:16 emphasizes the love of God through self-sacrifice, as Jesus laid down His life for us.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 John 3:22, we receive from God whatever we ask if we keep His commandments.
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:22 confirms that keeping His commandments allows us to receive from Him whatever we ask.

questions.question: True or False: 1 John 3:15 states that all murderers have eternal life abiding in them.
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:15 asserts that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him, highlighting the severity of hatred and sin.

theological.title: 1 John Chapter 3 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 John Chapter 3 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 John 3:5 teach about the sinlessness of Christ?
options: Christ was tempted but sinned not
Christ was partially sinful like us
Christ's sin was transferred to believers
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:5 explicitly states that 'in him is no sin,' affirming the doctrine of Christ's sinlessness.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification does 1 John 3:3 teach?
options: Hope in Christ purifies the believer
Sanctification is solely by human effort
Only priests are called to holiness
questions.correctAnswer: Hope in Christ purifies the believer
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:3 teaches that 'every man that hath this hope in him purifieth himself,' showing sanctification as a hopeful, ongoing process.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 John 3:9 teach about the nature of born-again believers and sin?
options: Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin
Believers can sin freely without consequence
Sin is unavoidable even for the born again
Born again status does not affect sin nature
questions.correctAnswer: Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:9 states that those born of God do not commit sin, emphasizing the transformative nature of regeneration.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 John 3:20 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:20 emphasizes that 'God is greater than our heart, and knoweth all things,' demonstrating His omniscience.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 John 3:16 specifically highlight?
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:16 highlights God's love, shown by Christ laying down His life for us.

questions.question: How does 1 John 3:11 connect to the theme of love in the broader biblical narrative?
options: It echoes the command to love one another from the Torah
It introduces a new commandment not found elsewhere
It contradicts the Old Testament teachings on neighborliness
It focuses solely on loving God rather than neighbors
questions.correctAnswer: It echoes the command to love one another from the Torah
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:11 references the enduring message 'that we should love one another,' consistent with biblical commands found in Leviticus 19:18 and Jesus' teachings.

questions.question: How does 1 John 3:8 relate to the redemptive-historical theme of Christ's victory over evil?
options: It teaches that the Son of God was manifested to destroy the works of the devil
It implies the devil has ultimate control over believers
It denies any conflict between Christ and Satan
It suggests that sin originated with humanity, not the devil
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that the Son of God was manifested to destroy the works of the devil
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:8 states clearly that the Son of God appeared to destroy the devil's works, aligning with the theme of Christ's redemptive victory.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 1 John 3:6 and 1 John 3:9 teach about the relationship between abiding in Christ and sin?
options: Abiding in Christ results in not sinning, as those born of God do not commit sin
Abiding in Christ has no effect on sinfulness
Sin is a necessary part of abiding in Christ
Only perfect people can abide in Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Abiding in Christ results in not sinning, as those born of God do not commit sin
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:6 and 3:9 together teach that those who abide in Christ and are born of God do not continue in sin.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 John 3:14 and 1 John 3:15 teach about love and eternal life?
options: Love for brothers is evidence of passing from death to life and necessary for eternal life
Hating a brother is permissible without losing eternal life
Love and eternal life are unrelated
Eternal life is guaranteed regardless of love for others
questions.correctAnswer: Love for brothers is evidence of passing from death to life and necessary for eternal life
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:14 and 3:15 show that loving the brethren confirms life and that hatred equates to murder, which excludes eternal life.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 John 3:23 and 1 John 3:24 teach about faith and obedience?
options: Belief in Jesus Christ and loving one another are commandments that result in abiding in God by the Spirit
Faith alone without love or obedience is sufficient to abide in God
Obedience is unrelated to faith in Jesus Christ
The Spirit dwells independently of faith or obedience
questions.correctAnswer: Belief in Jesus Christ and loving one another are commandments that result in abiding in God by the Spirit
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:23 and 3:24 combine to teach that faith in Christ and love lead to keeping commandments and abiding in God through the Spirit.

questions.question: Sceptics claim 1 John 3:6-10 teaches that Christians can never sin after regeneration. What does this passage actually teach?
options: True believers do not practice habitual, unrepentant sin because God’s seed remains in them
Christians are completely sinless in every action following regeneration
Sin is irrelevant to salvation once born of God
Believers must never struggle with sin or they are not saved
questions.correctAnswer: True believers do not practice habitual, unrepentant sin because God’s seed remains in them
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:6-10 teaches that those born of God do not commit sin in a habitual, defining way because God’s seed remains in them, not that they are utterly sinless.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 John 3:7 teach about righteousness and deception?
options: He that doeth righteousness is righteous as God is righteous
Righteousness is only an external appearance
Deception is permissible for the righteous
Righteousness is irrelevant to being known by God
questions.correctAnswer: He that doeth righteousness is righteous as God is righteous
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:7 warns believers not to be deceived and affirms that doing righteousness equates to being righteous as God is.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 John 3:22 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:22 teaches that 'whatsoever we ask, we receive of him, because we keep his commandments,' demonstrating God's faithfulness to His promises.

questions.question: What narrative arc does 1 John 3:1-2 advance regarding the believer's identity and future transformation?
options: Believers are called sons of God now and will be like Christ when He appears
Believers remain unchanged until the final judgment
Believers become gods themselves immediately upon faith
The world fully understands the believer's identity
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are called sons of God now and will be like Christ when He appears
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:1-2 presents the believer’s present identity as sons of God and future hope to be like Christ, reinforcing the redemptive transformation theme.

questions.question: What doctrine about love and compassion does 1 John 3:17 teach?
options: Love of God is absent if one refuses to help a needy brother
Love of God is expressed only in worship and prayer
Material wealth guarantees love for others
questions.correctAnswer: Love of God is absent if one refuses to help a needy brother
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:17 teaches that withholding compassion from a needy brother contradicts the presence of God’s love in one’s heart.
